question: A 65-year-old man presents to the physician for the evaluation of increasing dyspnea and swelling of the lower extremities over the past year. He has no cough. He also complains of frequent awakenings at night and excessive daytime sleepiness. He has no history of a serious illness. He takes no medications other than zolpidem before sleep. He is a 35-pack-year smoker. His blood pressure is 155/95 mm Hg. His BMI is 37 kg/m2. Oropharyngeal examination shows a small orifice and an enlarged tongue and uvula. The soft palate is low-lying. The examination of the nasal cavity shows no septal deviation or polyps. Symmetric pitting edema is seen below the knee, bilaterally. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Echocardiography shows a mildly dilated right ventricle and an elevated systolic pulmonary artery pressure with no abnormalities of the left heart. A ventilation-perfusion scan shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient’s symptoms?

options.opb: Heart failure with a preserved ejection fraction

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Obstructive sleep apnea" -> "intermittent hypoxia" -> "pulmonary vasoconstriction" -> "elevated pulmonary artery pressure" -> "right ventricular dilation" -> "dyspnea and lower extremity edema" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Obstructive sleep apnea" -> "intermittent hypoxia" -> "daytime sleepiness" -> "frequent awakenings at night" -> "excessive daytime sleepiness" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Obstructive sleep apnea" -> "obesity" -> "enlarged tongue and uvula" -> "airway obstruction during sleep" -> "intermittent hypoxia" -> "pulmonary hypertension" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Idiopathic pulmonary artery hypertension" -> "elevated pulmonary artery pressure" -> "right ventricular dilation" -> "dyspnea and lower extremity edema" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease" -> "smoking history" -> "dyspnea" -> "clear lungs on auscultation" -> "possible" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction" -> "hypertension" -> "dyspnea" -> "no left heart abnormalities" -> "possible" -> 65%
CHAIN: "Pulmonary thromboembolism" -> "elevated pulmonary artery pressure" -> "dyspnea" -> "clear ventilation-perfusion scan" -> "unclear" -> 50%
analysis: The patient's symptoms and examination findings are suggestive of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). The key indicators include excessive daytime sleepiness, frequent awakenings at night, obesity (BMI of 37 kg/m2), and oropharyngeal examination findings of a small orifice, enlarged tongue, uvula, and low-lying soft palate. These are classic features of OSA, which can lead to pulmonary hypertension and right heart strain, as evidenced by the echocardiography findings of a mildly dilated right ventricle and elevated systolic pulmonary artery pressure. The absence of left heart abnormalities and a normal ventilation-perfusion scan further support the diagnosis of OSA over other conditions such as COPD, heart failure, idiopathic pulmonary artery hypertension, or pulmonary thromboembolism.
